case_title.value: KRISHIKA LULLA & ORS. v. SHYAM VITHALRAO DEVKATIA&ANR.

quotes.text: KRISHIKA LULLA & ORS. v. SHYAM VITHALRAO DEVKATIA&ANR.

The respondent No. 1-Shyam Vithalrao Devkatta, filed a complaint being Criminal Case No. SW/332 of 2011 under Section 63 of the Copyright Act, later amended to add additional charges under Sections 406 and 420 read with Section 34 of the IPC, against five persons.
Criminal complaint for infringement of copyright is not tenable - Criminal proceedings are quashed

statutory_provisions.value: Copyright Act s.63; IPC s.406, s.420

quotes.text: Copyright Act, 1957 - ss. 13 and 63 - Penal Code, 1860 - ss. 406 and 420
The facts alleged by the respondent No. 1 can only be determined at the trial
The prosecution based on allegations of infringement of copyright in such a title is untenable

neutral_facts.value: The accused, who were involved in a film production, faced a criminal complaint alleging infringement of copyright in the title of a story synopsis. The complainant claimed that the title 'Desi Boys' was used by the accused for their film titled 'Desi Boyz', which was released in 2011. The complainant alleged that the title was the soul of his story and that its use by the accused constituted infringement. The accused argued that the title was not a literary work and therefore not protected by copyright. The case involved a dispute over whether the title of a story could be considered a literary work under copyright law. The accused sought to quash the criminal proceedings, which were dismissed by the trial court. The High Court also dismissed the applications to quash the complaint, stating that the facts would be determined at trial. The Supreme Court ultimately held that no copyright subsisted in the title of the story synopsis and that the criminal complaint was untenable.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that the respondent No.1, Shyam Vithalrao Devkatta, had claimed copyright in the title of the synopsis of a story 'Desi Boys' and that the appellants' film titled 'Desi Boyz' infringed this copyright.

quotes.text: The complainant/Respondent No.1 claims copyright in a synopsis of a story written by him with the title 'Desi Boys'. According to him, he had written a story with the title 'Desi Boys'.

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that there is no copyright in the title of a story or film, and therefore, the criminal complaint under Section 63 of the Copyright Act is not tenable.

quotes.text: Mr. Ramchandran, maintains that there is no copyright in the title of a story or for that matter a film and therefore, no complaint is tenable under Section 63 of the Copyright Act

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the principle that a title of a work, by itself, is not a subject of copyright and that copyright subsists only in original literary works as defined under Section 13 of the Copyright Act, 1957.

quotes.text: Copyright is a statutory right recognized and protected by The Copyright Act, 1957. On a plain reading of Section 13 of the Act, copyright subsists in inter-alia an original literary work.
